claims.claim: Reviewers report that navigating menus, controlling movement, and using quickbar abilities while moving are difficult or not user-friendly.

citations.review_text: Navigation and control are not user friendly

One of the best, if not the best Star Wars games I have ever played. The voice acting in this game is the best out of any MMORPG I have every played (and I have played dozens of them). Every Main Story quest and Side Quest that I have encounter so far at least has had high quality voice acting. My only real complaint is that it is hard to use the quickbar abilities and move around at the same time. I highly recommend changing the kebindings to something that feels comfortable (I personally use my numberpad on my keyboard for those). All that said, great game and one I wish to continue playing. Great job.

Disclaimer! I'm not particularly into MMOs and this is from someone who was essentially looking for a KOTOR3 experience - story driven RPG. This is absolutely not it. 

The story can be interesting at times, but the gameplay is so mind-numbingly boring that I abandoned after finishing a couple of planets (jedi knight, level 32). There's no gameplay nuance you just run around huge maps and kill damage-sponge enemies. That's literally it. As you level up you'll start avoiding enemies, because they're just annoying to fight and don't give enough exp to be worth the hassle, as unimmersive as it can get... There's some choice available during dialogue, but none whatsoever when it comes to gameplay and mission objectives, which imo is one of the main attractions of RPGs. No multiple ways to progress objectives, the same formula - fight or run past the mobs to the end-of-level boss, fight, have a convo, choose light/dark option rinse and repeat.

this is a good game, if you liked KOTOR. Tons of lore, 99.9% is voice acted. After a while I started skipping some side story dialog because I was predicting it in my head (i.e. "oh, than you so much for saving my brother!!!" and such).

claims.claim: Free-to-play users face a credit holding cap of 999,999 in their inventory.

citations.review_text:
It's wow, but star wars, i think the same engine or something extremely similar. But with nice cinematics and cool people. PVP and PVE, do whatever you want. 
The campaigns for all classes are ok, but the most 'fun' or story driven is the imperial agent i think.
You can play for achievements, crafting, cosmetics, collections, socialize a bit maybe... the big guilds talk a lot and are very helpful. 

The bad side is that if you are not a subscriber the game is slow and ofc you don't have access to most op and epic stuff in the game..... and one of the worst decisions the owners of the game had made is make 999.999 cap to hold credits in inventory ( can still put over 1mil in the legacy cargo hold )..... but that means a free user CANNOT buy, trade, unlock anything that is over 999.999 credits....... and there are a lot of good things to unlock over 1mil.........
I mean..... wth is this sht, let me hold over 1 mil in my inventory....... subscription every month is 14,15 euros....... and you only give a couple of free credits with the subscription, which is sht.....
But what can you expect from some money driven corpo......
All in all, the game is enjoyable, better if you have friends to play with

I truly love this game. Even though the graphics aren't currently as high-quality as the cinematics, the storylines have much to offer and all 8 origin stories are very different. I wish they would update it so that free-to-play had more to offer without as many limitations, however with the state of the game I understand. The combat system is very mmorpg style but once you get the rotations (what to press and when to press it) down, it gets pretty easy. The community is always helpful.

I've been playing SWTOR on and off for 15 years now. It's still a great game with hours of content for free. You really cant get much better value for a free to play game with hundreds of hours of Bioware storytelling. The worst part of F2P is the credit limit of 1mill but other than that it is highly worth playing if you are a fan of the MMO genre. The new devs are still updating and improving the game. New content is coming this year so it's a great time to return to the star wars universe.

Great MMO set in a story based game typical of BIOWARE, set in the star wars universe pre dating the film by about 3000 years, 8 completely unique stories - 1 for each class.

Star Wars: The Old Republic is one of the best story-driven MMORPGs ever created.

Set thousands of years before the movies, during the fascinating Old Republic era, the game benefits from one of the richest periods in the franchise's history. This is the same timeline that gave us legendary RPGs like Knights of the Old Republic, with Jedi, Sith, ancient conflicts, and a galaxy full of possibilities.

Its biggest strength is the storytelling. With fully voiced quests, memorable companions, and eight unique class stories, SWTOR feels much closer to a traditional BioWare RPG than a simple MMO. Each class offers a different fantasy and a genuinely different journey, whether you want to become a Jedi Knight, a Sith Lord, a bounty hunter, or a ruthless Imperial agent.

The gameplay follows a more traditional MMO formula and can feel dated today, but the amount of content, the atmosphere, and the focus on narrative make it stand out. The free-to-play model has some limitations, but there is still a lot to enjoy without a subscription.

If you miss the golden age of BioWare RPGs and want to explore one of the best eras of Star Wars lore, The Old Republic is absolutely worth experiencing.

claims.claim: Free-to-play accounts are restricted to a maximum of four character slots.

citations.review_text:
You can either be a war criminal who shoots/zaps/chokes whoever the hell they like or a goody two shoes who's worst crime is Defending themself against enemies who respawn anyway(Talk about plot armour). 
Side note- Unless your willing to spend some money for a subscription i personally wouldn't Advise it because while the character story's are good, your highly limited without buying a subscription and it's best to buy it for at least 1 month so that way you get all the DLC's and more characters so you can complete every class story without having to delete your other ones (The Limit for People who haven't subscribed for at least 1 month is 4 characters)

Star Wars: The Old Republic is a great MMO that stands out from the others with it's class storylines and singleplayer stories. Yes you can play with other people by doing dungeons, PVP, starfighter and more. The game doesn't pressure you into playing with other people. Each class has it's own storyline that you can complete while doing other quests. 

The Expansions also have a lot to offer, continuing the theme of singleplayer stories that your characters plays through. The dark side/light side mechanic is fun to and reminds me of older bioware games. Star Wars hasn't been good for awhile now and this game feels like the last real bastion of good star wars content.

The biggest downside I'll say for this game is that the Free to Play version is not very fun. You don't have sprint, you don't gain as much xp, you're money capped. So I would HIGHLY recommend you try out a month of subscription to see if this game is for you.
